newsitem.title: UK: French, North Americans top British tourism league.
newsitem.headline: French, North Americans top British tourism league.

text.p: Spending by overseas visitors to Britain rose five percent to 12.7 billion pounds ($20.5 billion) last year with North Americans and the French topping the tourist league, the British Tourist Authority said on Wednesday.
The number of visits to Britain rose eight percent to 26 million, helped by the country's style revival, the Channel Tunnel rail link and French people with an eye for a bargain in southern England.
"British fashion and Britpop are going down well with the French and the Eurostar has helped. Suddenly Britain is seen as much easier to get to," Isobel Coy, BTA spokeswoman said.
Coy said the French particularly were embarking on shopping trips for children's clothes and household goods. She attributed the slower growth in spending to Europeans taking more short breaks.
"There has been large growth in the European market and we are encouraging weekend breaks...People aren't spending so long in Britain but are making multiple visits," she said.
Tourists from the U.S. and Canada continued to form the mainstay of visitors to Britain, accounting for 3.9 million of all visits last year. The French were close behind, Coy said.
The BTA said the figures were encouraging, particularly after record 1995 tourism but it warned that the rate of growth could be difficult to maintain.
